sections.h2: What are your choices when selling a house in Schertz?
sections.html:
Three paths are open in Schertz: a listing with an agent, a do it yourself sale, or a cash purchase of the house in present condition. Repairs, deadlines and your tolerance for a lower price decide between them.

Schertz sits on the Bexar and Guadalupe county line, and the city later spread into Comal County. A single street can therefore fall under more than one county office, so confirm which county holds your parcel before you sign anything.

Collect each offer in writing and measure it against what an agent expects you would keep after commission and fix up costs.

sections.h2: How did Schertz grow from a rail stop into a suburb?
sections.html:
The Texas State Historical Association places Schertz on Farm Road 78, two miles southeast of Interstate 35 and nineteen miles west of Seguin. Sebastian Schertz kept a store there in 1875, when the Galveston, Harrisburg and San Antonio Railway built through.

A post office called Cutoff opened in 1884 and became Schertz in 1899. By 1890 the town had a cotton gin, a grocery and about 200 people, and by 1914 it added a church, a bank and a hotel.

Numbers barely moved for decades, holding near 350 from the early 1930s to the late 1950s. Then the interstate and San Antonio's outward growth changed everything. The town incorporated in 1958 with 351 residents, reached 2,281 within six years, 7,576 by 1988 and 10,555 in 1990.

The Handbook lists 18,694 residents in 2000 and 36,244 by 2015. A city that doubled in fifteen years has many newer subdivisions, and buyers often weigh a Schertz house against similar ones in nearby suburbs.

sections.h2: What does the City of Schertz offer residents that buyers notice?
sections.html:
The city's website promotes community events such as Schertz Hometown Harvest, held on the first Saturday of April, May, June, August, September, October and November. It also runs a public notices page for hearings and meetings, and a fire department poster contest for students from kindergarten through fourth grade.

None of that sets a price, but buyers visit the same pages you do. A seller can use the notices page to see whether a hearing affects a street or a zoning matter near the house, and can mention community events in a listing or a conversation with a buyer.

The city also published its Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget and tax rate. Buyers comparing Schertz with nearby cities will look at those rates, so ask the city for the figure that applies to your address instead of relying on a neighbor's bill.

sections.h2: Which county and school district serve your Schertz house?
sections.html:
Your tax statement answers it. Guadalupe County parcels go through the Guadalupe Appraisal District, whose member list includes the City of Schertz and Schertz-Cibolo-UC ISD. Parcels in Bexar or Comal County use those counties' districts.

Read the list of taxing units on the bill, because a buyer's agent will ask for it:

  • The appraisal district sets value and handles exemptions and protests.
  • The county tax office mails bills and takes payment.
  • The city sets its own rate; its website says the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget and tax rate were adopted.
  • The school district appears on the bill as its own line.

Ask the county tax office or the city what rate applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What building rules does Schertz enforce?
sections.html:
The City of Schertz Inspections Division issues building permits and registers contractors for construction within the city, and it reviews plans for work in the extraterritorial jurisdiction where that applies. Questions go to (210) 619-1750 or inspections@schertz.com. The division also investigates alleged building code complaints and supports the Unified Development Code.

Outdoor building work runs weekdays from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., and the city prohibits outdoor work on Sundays. Office hours at the division run 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. weekdays and 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. Saturdays.

Permits matter at sale time. If a room, deck or wall opening went in without one, a buyer's inspector may spot it. An as is cash buyer will likely price that risk, while a lender behind a conventional buyer may ask for a fix first.

sections.h2: What can Guadalupe Appraisal District do for a Schertz owner?
sections.html:
The district keeps a parcel search portal and online tools for homestead, disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, and printable forms are still available at its offices. Its Appraisal Review Board hears appeals at the main office in Seguin, and a taxpayer liaison officer attends on hearing days. The liaison can be reached by phone at 830.303.3313 extension 309.

The district also warns about mail. Since late December 2025, USPS postmarks in Texas reflect the date of automated processing instead of the day you drop an item off. Anyone filing a time sensitive paper form should take it to a post office counter for a manual postmark.

If you are unsure whether to call the district or the tax office, remember the split: the district handles values, exemptions and protests, and the tax office handles bills and payments.

sections.h2: How do Texas homestead breaks apply to a Schertz house?
sections.html:
Property value is fixed on January 1, and each year's tax lien starts the same day. These figures are as the Comptroller prints them:

Homestead relief that can apply to a Schertz house (Texas Comptroller)
BenefitWho gets itAs printed
School homestead exemptionOwner living in the home$140,000
Extra school exemptionAge 65 or more, or disabled$60,000
Appraisal capHomestead owner10 percent a year
School tax ceilingAge 65 or more, or disabledTotal annual school tax cannot rise

Bills arrive around October 1, and January 31 is the usual last day to pay. Any balance left at closing is subtracted from what you receive, which is why an early payoff figure from the county helps.

sections.h2: What if you are behind on the mortgage or the taxes in Schertz?
sections.html:
A Texas lender cannot hold a foreclosure sale until a notice of sale goes out, and the auction falls on a first Tuesday. Selling privately beforehand can keep the equity that a foreclosure might hand to junior lien holders first.

Unpaid taxes pile on costs. Charges start February 1, and the penalty climbs to 12 percent by July 1. Some collectors allow installment plans for a residence homestead, so call the tax office early.

sections.h2: Can you sell a Schertz house that has a tenant?
sections.html:
You can. A buyer may take the property with the lease in place, or you may end the tenancy before listing. Removal runs through written notice and a justice court case, and a writ of possession follows a final judgment.

A paying tenant who keeps the place tidy can keep rent flowing until closing. Where rent has stopped, a buyer who accepts the house as is may handle the removal after closing.

sections.h2: How are deeds and probate houses handled in Schertz?
sections.html:
The county clerk files the deed, once a notary or other authorized officer has witnessed the signature. Because Schertz crosses county lines, confirm which clerk before you visit.

Inherited houses follow the estate's route:

  • A will that went through probate leads to an executor's deed or a court order.
  • A muniment of title can pass a house when the estate owes only real estate liens.
  • An heirship affidavit is a sworn statement placed with the clerk, but a buyer or title company can decline it.

A title company can say which route fits before you list.

faqs.a: Three: Bexar, Comal and Guadalupe. The Handbook of Texas puts the town on the Bexar and Guadalupe line and says it spread into Comal County.

faqs.q: What if work on my Schertz house lacked a permit?
faqs.a: You can still sell, but expect questions. The Inspections Division issues permits, and its number is (210) 619-1750.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax at a Schertz closing?
faqs.a: The contract sets the split, often by days of ownership. Get the amount owed from the county tax office before closing day.

faqs.q: What happens after the January 31 tax deadline?
faqs.a: The bill is delinquent from February 1, and penalty and interest begin. The penalty grows each month until it hits 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: Must a Schertz house be repaired before a cash sale?
faqs.a: Often no. Cash buyers frequently take houses in present condition. Weigh that offer against an agent's projection after repairs and commission.
